newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wool faces mixed market in 1997 - IWS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wool faces mixed market in 1997 - IWS.

text.p: Reasonable wool apparel sales are occurring in the crucial northern hemisphere autumn/winter retail season but sales in continental Europe continue to lag, the International Wool Secretariat (IWS) said.

With higher volumes of wool now moving into the pipeline and greater fashion interest in wool, wool prices would largely depend on how quickly northern hemisphere retailers could sell their current autumn/winter apparel, the IWS said in its monthly market briefing. Wool apparel was reportedly selling well in Britain and in the Netherlands, especially knitwear, it said.

After a slowdown in 1995, consumer expenditure in Britain was picking up strongly in 1996, largely because of cuts in direct taxation, falling unemployment and payouts from building society mergers, the briefing said.
There were now opportunities to raise prices in market segments in Brtiain which were performing particularly well, in sharp contrast with many markets elsewhere in Europe, it said.
Wool looked set to impriovce its market position further in Britain in 1997, it said.
In Germany, wool apparel sales picked up in October.
But elsewhere in Europe there were few positive reports, despite a reasonable wool offer and the early arrival of cold weather, the IWS said.

Personal consumption in continental Europe was expected to show average growth of only 1.6 percent in 1997, with the large Italian market lagging behind France and Germany. In contrast, growth in Britain was forecast to reach 3.7 percent.

In Japan, wool apparel was selling reasonably well, particularly women's knitwear and coats and men's suits in the upper market. Menswear, however, was not performing to expectations in the volume market, it said.

Japanese consumer sentiment and spending remained fragile and personal consumption is forecast to rise by a slower 2.4 percent in 1997, it said. Apparel retail sales in the U.S. were strong into the 1996 holiday season, with wool reported to be doing well in knitwear and womenswear, it said.
U.S. consumption should expand in 1997 although more slowly than in the 1996 election year, the IWS said.

Overall personal consumption growth in Western Europe, Japan and the U.S. were forecast at 2.2 percent for 1997, unchanged on the 1996 average and below the 2.5 percent-3.0 percent growth generally needed before significant expenditure on apparel
occurred in developed markets, the briefing said.
